headline: Highest risk is medium: Great Expectations can read and write validation files while the paired awesome-python repo is a non-runnable collection, so interaction risks are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default communication channel is documented between awesome-python and great_expectations. Agent A is a non-runnable collection with no I/O surfaces; agent B has file surfaces, but nothing shows B ingesting A's outputs by default. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent B is configured to parse content from agent A as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue.
Review any file-import step before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B touches data sources, validation results, and documentation, while agent A is only a curated Python-links collection and has no data classes or network egress. There is no documented shared workspace or secret handling, so leakage is limited to an unusual local file-sharing setup rather than a default path.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace, B could read files associated with A.
IF sensitive data is placed into B's validation inputs, those artifacts may appear in B's outputs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Do not place sensitive files in the shared repo.
Restrict B's input paths to a dedicated folder.
Check outputs for accidental file echoes before sharing.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation in the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or network capabilities documented, while agent B can install packages and write files under its file surfaces. Because A is non-runnable and lacks mutable capabilities, direct write-write conflict is not shown; only a small conflict risk exists if an operator manually couples them to the same directory.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF B is allowed to install packages into an environment A also depends on, environment drift may occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Pin B's environment before running it.
Avoid letting B modify shared project files.
Snapshot the workspace before any package install.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations can produce validation results and documentation, but awesome-python is a static collection and does not act on outputs. There is no evidence that B treats A's output as authoritative or that A generates operational facts for B, so cascading error is limited unless an operator manually feeds A-derived content into B.
conditions: IF A-derived text is manually copied into B as validation input, B may propagate that content.
IF B is configured to auto-generate downstream actions from validation results, errors could cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of any copied content.
Do not use A as a source of factual assertions for B.
Separate documentation browsing from validation runs.
Add a verification checklist before publishing B outputs.
requires-engineering: add source-traceability checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. Agent A is a public open-source collection with no data classes touched, and agent B handles data quality tests, validation results, and documentation without secrets or residency claims. The rubric's residency and regulated-data triggers are not present in either profile.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into B's inputs, compliance review is required.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency-constrained policy not shown here, reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document the data classes allowed in B.
Review deployment residency before use.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
